findings.skill_statement: SKILL.md:1468-1469 sends the reader to 'the re-sweep cadence section's closing note' for round 8's driver-invocation `[U]`. The section named resolves uniquely at C4 (`## The re-sweep cadence and the six-case confidence statement (round 8, measured)`, SKILL.md:1015, span 1015-1161), and the token is inside that span — but not in a closing note: the only `[U]` occurrence in the whole span is SKILL.md:1024, the last line of the section's LEAD paragraph (1017-1024, '... the round boundary; whether any fleet driver would ever invoke the command with / no lane acting stays [U].'). The section's closing content carries no token: 1157-1158 '- **Unknown in all six:** coordinated rewrites; cross-host stability; the 50 % / crossover; the two round-8 notes' own unknowns.' and 1159-1160 '- **Read the method, not the rate** - at six cases the constant remains the / survivor taxonomy and the composition rule, not the headline percentage.' The phrase 'closing note' occurs nowhere else in SKILL.md (single occurrence, this line), so it is not a page-defined alias for a lead paragraph; read literally the locator names a place where the cited `[U]` is absent. Not a C4 regression: the section is byte-identical at C** 5b703c6f and C4 a977394 (sha256 6600bf90bbde2f88f4df2f7908f919d5725e42735e589414509ba43c87cf7a7d at both), so the wording predates the C4 fix and was left untouched by it.
